challenges.name: user-id-label-review-quiz
challenges.title: Review the AI's metric
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the review of the AI-written submissions counter: the bill after it shipped with a dashboard that hides the labels, and the proposed fix.

questions.question:
The change the AI assistant wrote for "add a metric so we can see which learners submit the most":

+ submissions.add(1, { user_id: req.userId, url: req.url, method: req.method, status: String(status) });

Metrics vendor usage for codedev-api:
         active series   monthly cost
before   41,200          $310
after    128,900         $970

count(codedev_submissions_total) => 87,400

The team dashboard only shows totals and uses:
sum without (user_id, url) (rate(codedev_submissions_total[5m]))

Statement: "Because the dashboard query removes user_id and url with sum without (...), those series are not stored, so the bill will drop back once this panel is saved."
questions.explanation: False. Labels are attached when the counter is recorded, in the API process: every combination of user_id, url, method and status is exported, scraped, indexed and stored as its own series before any query runs. sum without (...) aggregates at query time; it changes what the panel shows, not what the backend keeps, and it even makes every refresh of the panel read the 87,400 series. To stop paying for them you have to stop recording the labels (or drop them in the SDK with a View, or in the collector, before export). The misconception is that a query decides what is stored.

True. Each label now has a small, fixed set of values: one route template for this handler, one method and at most five status classes, so the counter has at most about five series whether CodeDev has a thousand learners or a million. The learner id has not disappeared: it moved to an event, where one row per submission is the normal shape and where a query like "top 10 learners this week" is cheap. The misconception is that dropping user_id from the metric means losing the per-learner answer; it means asking the store that is designed for it.

challenges.name: spot-the-ai-mistake-user-id-label
challenges.title: Spot the AI Mistake: user_id as a metric label
hints: How many different values can user_id take on CodeDev next year? And url? Multiply them with the other labels: that is how many series the metrics backend has to keep for this one counter. Which of the four labels have a small, fixed set of values?

Look at the object passed to this.submissions.add in onSubmission: each key is a label. The request already carries a value that names the route without the ids, and the status can be reduced to its class. Then look at the AnalyticsSink class at the bottom of the file: it already knows how to count events per user, so topLearners does not need the counter at all.

A similar case with other data: a counter of video plays labelled { video_id, viewer_id, quality } grows with every viewer. Keep { quality } (and the player version) on the counter, which tells you how many plays fail or buffer, and send { name: "video_played", userId: viewerId, properties: { videoId } } to the event pipeline, where "most active viewers" is a group-by over events. Anonymous viewers stay in the counter but do not become a fake user in the events.

tests.name: Counts submissions and finds the learners who submit the most
Ties are ordered by learner id and top(n) returns at most n learners
tests.expected:
top 1: u_binh 2
top 2: u_binh 2, u_dung 2
top 10: u_binh 2, u_dung 2, u_an 1
total: 5

tests.name: Series use the route template, the method and the status class only
10,000 learners: the counter keeps a bounded number of series
tests.expected:
series: 3
  {method="POST",route="/submissions",status_class="2xx"} 17600
  {method="POST",route="/submissions",status_class="4xx"} 1600
  {method="POST",route="/submissions",status_class="5xx"} 800
total: 20000
top 3: u0 2, u1 2, u10 2

tests.name: Every submission of a signed-in learner reaches the analytics sink

analytics: 3 submission_created events from 2 learners
  last: u_an c_18 500

  last: u299 c_11 202
top 2: u0 3, u1 3
